title: CDF Update…. CHAMA TOWN COUNCIL ENHANCES HEALTH CENTER LIGHTING ACROSS CHAMA NORTH CONSTITUENCY
body_text: CDF Update…. CHAMA TOWN COUNCIL ENHANCES HEALTH CENTER LIGHTING ACROSS CHAMA NORTH CONSTITUENCY Chama, Zambia – In a major boost to healthcare, Chama Town Council has enhanced lighting in 19 health centers in Chama North Constituency, utilizing the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), the Vitalite lighting system has four efficient bulbs at a cost of K 5,825 per unit. The council has successfully procured and installed the Vitalite lighting system, which features four energy-efficient bulbs, ensuring better lighting, particularly at maternity annexes. title: CHAMA DISTRICT LAUNCHES THE FIRST INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT PLAN
body_text: Chama, Zambia – In a significant move towards enhancing the quality of life for its residents, the Minister of Local Government and Rural Development, Honorable Gary Nkombo, has formally launched the Integrated Development Plan (IDP) for Chama district. The event was marked by a speech from Dr. Lewis Mwape, the Deputy Permanent Secretary for Eastern Province, who emphasized the IDP’s critical role in the district’s transformation. The IDP is designed with the ambitious goal of improving living standards in Chama by the year 2035. Key initiatives outlined in the plan include the construction of new schools, upgrading of roads, expanding access to clean water, improving health services, promoting income-generating activities, and tackling pressing issues such as poverty, nutrition, early marriages, gender-based violence, and environmental sustainability. During the launch, Hon. Nkombo urged local authorities to take proactive steps in implementing the IDP rather than allowing it to become just another document filed away. He stressed the importance of collaboration between local authorities, Members of Parliament, and Councillors, who represent the interests of the community. “It is essential that these elected officials are actively involved in the IDP process to ensure projects accurately reflect the needs of the people and to avoid repeating past mistakes of implementing projects that do not serve the community,” he stated. Hon. Nkombo described the IDP as a strategic framework that will guide the local authority’s developmental agenda and foster cooperation with key stakeholders to achieve the outlined objectives. Chama Town Council Chairperson Gift Kumwenda echoed this sentiment, affirming the council’s dedication to providing exceptional services and making a meaningful impact through the IDP from 2025 to 2035. He noted that the government’s recent increase in the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) from K1.6 million to K36.1 million per constituency presents a vital opportunity for the realization of impactful projects. Additionally, Chama Town Council Secretary Francis Muzyani expressed heartfelt appreciation for the team’s hard work and expertise in developing the IDP, highlighting their dedication as crucial to the plan’s success.

title: GOVERNMENT DISBURSES K 7,436,841 FOR CDF SKILLS DEVELOPMENT
body_text: Chama Town Council is pleased to announce the disbursement of K 7,436,841 specifically for the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) skills development programs aimed at students from various colleges. This initiative is designed to enhance vocational training and provide the youth with crucial skills needed enabling them to become self-employed. This disbursement follows a thorough tour conducted by Chama Town Council officers, who visited the institutions where the students are currently enrolled. The purpose of this tour was to conduct due diligence, ensuring that the colleges meet required standards, confirming student arrival, and auditing the institutions ahead of the financial disbursement. In Chama North Constituency, the Council has disbursed funding for 164 first-time students amounting to K 3,568,039 and 14 returning students K 363,870. In Chama South Constituency, the Council has disbursed funding for 158 first-time students amounting to K 3,009,139 and 17 returning students K 558,900. The Council is dedicated to supporting the youth in their educational endeavours, believing that equipping them with relevant skills will contribute to economic growth and development in our nation.

title: CHAMA TOWN COUNCIL HOLDS SUCCESSFUL BUDGET STAKEHOLDERS CONSULTATIVE MEETING
body_text: Chama Town Council convened a highly productive stakeholders consultative meeting today at the Council Chamber, marking a significant step in transparent governance and strategic planning for the district’s development. The meeting, attended by key government officials including the District Administrative Officer Mr. Weston Phiri, who represented the District Commissioner, and Director of Engineering Eng. Khuda Khati on behalf of the Council Secretary, reviewed the performance of the current fiscal year’s budget and discussed the upcoming 2026 budget review. Financial Performance and Key Highlights As of June 30, 2025, Chama District demonstrated robust revenue performance, particularly in local revenue collection, despite the district’s expansive size of 17,164 square kilometers, making it the largest in Eastern Province. The district, sharing boundaries with Musalangu GMA and stretching into Muchinga Province, is rich in natural resources with a thriving agriculture and tourism sector. In terms of expenditure, the district has maintained prudent financial management, supporting ongoing projects and services. The meeting also provided an update on the debt status, indicating manageable levels that do not impede future growth. Cash for Work programs are ongoing, aiming to improve infrastructure and create employment opportunities. Development Projects and Administrative Updates The council reviewed the progress of CDF-funded projects, which continue to enhance community infrastructure. Council staff levels are being maintained to ensure effective service delivery, while internal audit reports reflect a high standard of compliance and accountability. The district’s assets managed by the local authority include various public facilities and infrastructure, with a list of outstanding court cases currently under review. Notably, some retirees who contributed to district development are yet to be paid their pensions, a matter highlighted for expedited resolution. Wildlife and Land Use Chama’s vast unutilized land, much of which falls within a Game Management Area (GMA), offers significant opportunities for expansion in agriculture particularly rice, maize, groundnuts, and cotton and wildlife tourism, which remains a key economic driver. Stakeholder Engagement and Future Outlook The meeting emphasized the importance of stakeholder participation in shaping Chama’s economic trajectory. Discussions also covered the need to optimize land use, enhance revenue collection, and streamline administrative processes to maximize the district’s potential. Chama District’s strategic location and rich natural resources position it for substantial growth, especially in agriculture and tourism. The council’s commitment to transparency and inclusive planning ensures that community needs and development priorities remain at the forefront.

Mr Kumwenda said this during the last full council meeting held at the council chambers in Chama district which marked the end of his five-year tenure, ahead of this year’s August general elections. The outgoing Council Chairperson said there are many projects that have been completed across the district but not yet operational. “It is important that these projects are handed over and put to use without delay. They risk being vandalized if they continue being idle, and this will not benefit the intended communities,” he said. And Mr Kumwenda has thanked the Chama Town Council Management, District Administration Office and the two Members of Parliament in the district for their dedication and unwavering support during his term. Meanwhile, Chama Town Council Secretary (CS) Francis Muzyani who was represented by the Director of Planning, Sydney Chipili, thanked the outgoing CS and his councillors for their dedication to duty in ensuring the local authority delivered on its mandate. He said the local authority had compiled a status report on all capital projects under the Constituency Development Fund and other government programmes, and that steps are being taken to fast-track commissioning processes. The meeting brought together councillors from the district’s 24 wards, heads of departments, and invited stakeholders to review the council’s performance and outstanding matters. title: Chama Gives Out K16m In CDF Grants And Loans
body_text: By Christopher Miti Chama Town council has disbursed over 16 million Kwacha Constituency Development Fund loans and grants to both Chama North and Chama South constituencies. The local authority has also drilled 20 boreholes, constructed classroom blocks and staff houses in various schools across the two constituencies. Eastern Province Minister PETER PHIRI, who commissioned the projects, says CDF has enabled the local people to embark on community driven developments. Mr PHIRI says it is gratifying that the priorities of the people are identified and implemented. Chama District Commissioner YOBE GOMA says the increment of CDF will help exploit the economic potential of the district. And Council Chairperson GIFT KUMWENDA has appealed to the government to consider positioning relief food in strategic areas before the onset of the rains. Meanwhile, Chief LUNDU, who spoke on behalf of the traditional leaders said the increment of CDF by the government is historic. The district has an area of approximately 17,472.8 km2 (6,750 square miles) and It is situated between longitudes 31.450 and 32.300 East and latitudes 13.800 and 14.450 South with altitudes from 350 m to 640 m above sea level as well as Muchinga escarpment that rises to 1,200 m above sea level. Chama District is surrounded by six (6) Districts (Mafinga, Isoka, Chinsali, Shiwang’andu, Mpika, and Chasefu Districts) and an international boundary with Malawi on its Eastern side. Demographics In Chama district, the population has been gradually growing from 55,172 people in 1990 to 74,890 in 2000 with an annual average growth rate of 3.1 percent. Further, the population grew from 103,894 in 2010 to 140,784 in 2022 (CSO, 2022) with an annual growth rate of 2.5%. The population for the number of females was estimated at 71,616 while the overall estimated population for males was estimated at 68,710. In comparison to the 2010 census Chama still had a higher number of females compared to males, which was at 48.1 for males per and 51.9 percent for females. Physical Features The district has one major river namely the Luangwa River that flows from the north down to the south. The river network also includes other rivers flowing into the luangwa river, which are the Luumbu, Kalinkhu, Mbwata, Kamphemba in the north, and Bazimu, Lupamazi, Lunzi, Luelo, Luvila, and Lundazi in the south. Chama district maintains one (1) National Forest and four (4) local forest reserves namely Lundazi National Forest, Makutu, Chire, Fibale, and Pondo local forests covering a total of 333,566 Hectares In addition, the district boasts of hosting the Musalangu game management area which home to over 100 different mammal species Luangwa River in Chikwa Chiefdom Chama-Lundazi Forest Contact Information CIVIC CENTRE P.O.
